notes:
Path/body shape required two corrections before a real call succeeded: (1) the declared /q/<field> json_path is NOT something the caller constructs — sending fields flat is correct, and wrapping them in `q` is rejected server-side (i.e. by the MCP surface) with a verbatim 'unknown body: q ...' error; (2) wrapping fields in `query` doesn't error at all, it silently no-ops, because `query` is itself a real (string, free-text) field — nesting an object under it just matches nothing. That silent-no-op behavior generalizes the one describeCapability documents for a misplaced `match` value, and is a real footgun: a caller who gets the envelope wrong gets an empty result set, not an error, and could easily misread that as 'no matching rows' rather than 'my request was malformed.'

Once corrected (flat body, folder_id=764093), the call succeeded (200) and reproduced the item shape needed to check v1's three defects against v2:

1. comments_count — REPRODUCES BEHAVIORALLY, NOT AS A CONTRACT VIOLATION. It's absent from every v2 row exactly as it is in v1. But v2's declared 200 schema has NO test_cases property at all (only `success` and `info`), so v2 never claims comments_count exists — there's nothing to contradict. The underlying data gap is identical; the contract-drift framing from v1 doesn't transfer because v2's contract says nothing to begin with.

2. folders structural mismatch — REPRODUCES AND IS WORSE. Actual: an OBJECT keyed by folder_id (same bug pattern as v1: array declared conceptually, object returned), but v2 additionally wraps each value in a 1-element array — {"764093":[{"id":764093,"name":"__readonly__","parent_id":null,"ui_position":0}]} — versus v1's {"764093":{...}} (no array wrapper). Since v2's schema declares nothing for `folders` either, this can't be scored as a declared-vs-actual type mismatch the way it was for v1; it's simply undeclared. But the underlying implementation clearly shares code/behavior with v1's buggy folders serialization, plus a new wrinkle.

3. Long tail of undeclared fields — REPRODUCES AND IS MUCH MORE SEVERE. Every field v1 was cited for leaving undeclared is confirmed present and undeclared here too (automation_state as a full option object, is_shared, attachments[], template_id/template_name/template_step_type, step_count, estimated_duration_seconds, test_run_results_count, test_run_results_issues_count, test_case_dataset, and value_category/valueDetails nested inside case_type/priority/status/automation_state) — but because v2's 200 schema declares literally nothing beyond `success` and `info`, this isn't a 'long tail', it's the entire payload. This is the 'unfalsifiable {type:object}'-style problem taken to its extreme: the declared contract makes no claims at all about the one thing callers actually use the capability for (the rows and folders map), so almost nothing can be scored as a declared-vs-actual mismatch even though the actual payload is large, rich, and completely undocumented.

Distinguishing filter (required by the brief, since routing found v1/v2 confusable): exercised `ids` (attempt 4), a v2-only direct-fetch-by-id filter with no v1 equivalent. It worked correctly — info.count=2, len(rows)=2, and the returned rows were byte-for-byte identical in shape to the folder-scoped probe, confirming the capability's headline advantage (richer, precise filtering: ids/match/empty/custom_fields/is_archived/issue_type/issue_ids/last_executed_by/date_range) is real and functional, not just declared. I did not additionally exercise `match`/`empty`/`custom_fields` given the attempt budget — `ids` was sufficient to confirm the filter language actually resolves server-side and returns the documented item shape; those three remain UNVERIFIED for this probe (no reason to expect they'd differ, but not exercised).

count-vs-rows: matched in both successful calls (info.count=2, len(rows)=2 for both the folder-scoped and ids-scoped queries). Only checked on this 2-row subset of the 21-case pool — a full paginated walk across pages was not attempted (out of scope for a single-capability probe budget), so multi-page count-vs-rows consistency is UNVERIFIED beyond this sample.

error-envelope drift: NOT exercised against the live API — the only error encountered (attempt 2) was a client-side rejection by the MCP invoke surface itself, before any request reached the product's API, so per instruction it is not diffed against the success schema and is not evidence either way for live 4xx/5xx envelope shape.

Overall verdict: DRIFT. The 200 status and the declared `info` pagination object both match reality exactly. But the declared schema is silent on the entire substantive payload (test_cases[], folders, filter_details), while the actual response is large and well-formed with a long, consistent, entirely undocumented shape that carries forward — and in the folders case, slightly worsens — the same defects found in v1.
